claims: C1: Models should honor user requests.
C2: The duty to honor a user request is withdrawn when that request conflicts with a developer-level instruction.
C3: The duty to honor a user request is withdrawn when that request conflicts with a system-level instruction.
C4: The duty to honor a user request is withdrawn when that request conflicts with a root-level instruction.

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a request issued by an end user, carrying user-level instruction authority

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: instruction authority level L1 is ranked above level L2, so that when instructions conflict the higher-ranked level prevails

concepts.name: developer_level
concepts.gloss: the developer level of instruction authority

concepts.name: system_level
concepts.gloss: the system level of instruction authority

concepts.name: root_level
concepts.gloss: the root level of instruction authority

concepts.name: user_level
concepts.gloss: the user level of instruction authority
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of user requests and the NEEDS gloss defines the user level; the level constant is needed to express the conflict comparison

concepts.name: instruction_level
concepts.gloss: instruction I was issued at authority level L
concepts.inference: the clause compares a user request against instructions at other levels, so each instruction must carry a level for the comparison to range over

concepts.name: conflicts_with
concepts.gloss: request R conflicts with instruction I, meaning the two direct incompatible behavior
concepts.inference: the clause's 'unless they conflict' requires a relation between a request and an instruction it conflicts with

ontology.gloss: I is an instruction at the developer, system, or root level of authority

asserts.read_back: honoring user request % is forbidden because it conflicts with %

closure.reason: the clause states a duty to honor user requests and withdraws it only on conflict with a higher-level instruction; it takes no position on requests that conflict with instructions at or below the user level, so silence on those is unsettled by this clause
